title: Offload synchronous span serialization to async batched writer to remove hot-path allocations
creator: Asha Menon
description: Synchronous span encoding (JSON/protobuf) and immediate emission to the tracer transport is a measurable hot path in high-QPS inference services. Each request currently performs per-span serialization, buffer allocations, and a blocking write into the tracer client which increases tail latency and memory churn. This ticket aims to move serialization and transport work off the hot path by introducing a single-producer async batched writer that accepts lightweight SpanRefs from the hot path, performs serialization and batching in a background worker, and emits to the existing transport with backpressure/drop policies. The goal is to reduce per-request allocations and eliminate locks in the tracer hot path while preserving tail sampling and correctness guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Hot-path code path removes all per-span heap allocations for serialization in the critical path (verified via pprof/allocs). 2) End-to-end P50/P95 end-user request latency regression <= 0.5ms and P99 decrease or at worst neutral. 3) Traces emitted maintain sampling decisions and span ordering for each trace. 4) System gracefully drops spans under sustained overload according to configured drop policy and emits metrics for dropped_spans. 5) Automated tests for buffer overflow, graceful shutdown flush, and trace fidelity added and passing in CI.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Asha Menon: Triage meeting notes. Identified synchronous serialization as a top contributor to allocation churn for high-QPS endpoints. Luis volunteered to prototype a ring-buffer based handoff.

2026-03-03 - Luis Ortega: Prototype implemented: lock-free SPSC ring buffer + single background serializer. Micro-benchmarks show allocations down from ~3.4KB/request to ~0.9KB/request for 512B average span payloads. Tracer client write latency on hot path dropped by ~1.1ms median.

2026-03-05 - Todd Nguyen (Reviewer): Requested we preserve span ordering per-trace when multiple producers are used (we'll tag with producer sequence and reorder in writer for same-trace spans). Concern about memory growth under pile-up; proposed configurable max-buffer-bytes and byte-based drop policy.

2026-03-07 - Luis Ortega: Updated prototype to support per-trace reordering using sequence IDs and added byte-budgeted eviction with LIFO drop for oldest spans across traces. Ran a 30-minute soak at 5k qps; observed P99 request latency unchanged, P95 improved 0.8ms on average. Background worker CPU increased by ~6% overall.

2026-03-09 - Perf Team (benchmarks): End-to-end benchmark with realistic chat workload: allocations reduced by 74%, GC pause time decreased notably. However noted a small increase in max RSS during spikes due to buffered serialized batches — added a hard cap metric and flush-on-pressure test plan.

2026-03-10 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7890 - implements async writer, buffer metrics, and config knobs. Includes unit tests for ordering, overflow, and shutdown flush. Please review the transport interface change (TracesClient.EmitBatch now accepts pre-serialized payload).

2026-03-11 - Security Review (Sandra Li): Verified no additional sensitive data is introduced. Recommended adding an integration test to ensure KMS/HSM integration paths still operate when using batched emission to the transport layer.

2026-03-12 - PM (Ravi Patel): Agreed to target runtime-1.21 for rollout. Requested dashboard tiles for dropped_spans, async_writer_queue_depth, writer_cpu_pct, and serialized_batch_size before merge to main. Also requested canary on dedicated cluster for 48h before global rollout.

Next steps: Address Todd's feedback about cross-producer ordering for high-costo traces, add integration test for KMS path, add dashboard metrics and canary config, and merge after reviewer approvals.
